阪.meaning: Climbers race to plant their <part>pennant</part> on the hilltop, but a grumpy goat is <part>anti</part> visitors and butts each one back down. Only the slowest climber, who brought carrots, reaches the <kanji>heights</kanji>.
阪.on: The goat likes its carrots dipped in <sound>hon</sound>ey.
阪.kun: The fastest climber rolls back down the slope, past a <sound>sa</sound>lsa stall, and stops against a parked <sound>ca</sound>r.

雅.meaning: A huge walrus with one chipped <part>tusk</part> lets a <part>sparrow</part> hop onto it, then bows like a butler and offers it a crumb. The tiny bird bows back. Even a walrus can be <kanji>gracious</kanji>.
雅.on: The crumb is from a slice of <sound>ga</sound>rlic bread.
雅.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>?' chirps the sparrow, and flies off across the <sound>ya</sound>rd with a <sound>bee</sound>.

鈴.meaning: A shepherd who has lost her voice gives the flock its <part>orders</part> by jingling: one jingle for 'eat', two for 'home', three for 'wolf!'. All of it comes from one <part>gold</part> <kanji>small bell</kanji> on her wrist.
鈴.on: Far across the hills, the sheep come running at every <sound>rin</sound>g.
鈴.kun: The wolf, scared off, sulks over a <sound>su</sound>shi roll and a sour yu<sound>zu</sound>.

扶.meaning: A tiny tugboat can't drag a giant ship off the rocks alone. A <part>husband</part> on the pier ties the ship's <part>anchor</part> to his rowing boat and rows with all his might beside it. Slowly, together, they pull it free: the ship got its <kanji>aid</kanji>.
扶.on: Afterwards he collapses onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton on deck.
扶.kun: The grateful crew bring him a <sound>ta</sound>rt and a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi.

蚕.meaning: A little <part>insect</part> munches mulberry leaves and dreams of the <part>heavens</part>. It spins itself a shiny, cloud-white cocoon, hoping to float up into the sky. Instead a weaver unwinds its cloud into a pillowcase, and the moth flutters off to find the sky elsewhere: the <kanji>silkworm</kanji>.
蚕.on: The moth lands on a <sound>sun</sound>dae, mistaking the cream for a cloud.
蚕.kun: It chases a <sound>ki</sound>te all afternoon, then naps on a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala.

奴.meaning: A <part>woman</part> at the fair bets nobody can tie a <part>pretzel</part> into a knot with their tongue. A bloke in a flat cap steps up and does it twice, then bows. Nobody knows his name; everyone just calls him 'that <kanji>guy</kanji>'.
奴.on: Next year he does it while riding a <sound>do</sound>lphin.
奴.kun: '<sound>Ya</sound>, easy!' he grins, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and the knot comes undone.

伐.meaning: A knight hangs her cloak on a <part>coat hook</part>, grips her <part>spear</part> and charges the giant oak blocking the castle road. Hack, hack, hack: by sunset the oak tips over with a groan. She is the first knight ever to <kanji>fell</kanji> a tree.
伐.on: A gold <sound>but</sound>ton pops off her armour from the effort.
伐.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird nesting in the oak tumbles out as it falls and lands on her helmet.
